rules.query:
title: Alternate PowerShell Hosts - PowerShell Module
id: 64e8e417-c19a-475a-8d19-98ea705394cc
status: test
description: Detects alternate PowerShell hosts potentially bypassing detections looking for powershell.exe
references:
    - https://threathunterplaybook.com/hunts/windows/190610-PwshAlternateHosts/notebook.html
author: Roberto Rodriguez @Cyb3rWard0g
date: 2019-08-11
modified: 2026-11-28
tags:
    - attack.execution
    - attack.t1059.001
logsource:
    product: windows
    category: ps_module
    definition: 0ad03ef1-f21b-4a79-8ce8-e6900c54b65b
detection:
    selection:
        ContextInfo|contains: '*'
    filter_powershell:
        # This filter covers the following use cases
        #   - When powershell is called directly from commandline via keyword powershell or powershell.exe
        #   - Or called via path but not with full "".exe". Example: C:\Windows\SysWOW64\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell
        ContextInfo|contains:
            - '= powershell' # Host Application=...powershell.exe or Application hote=...powershell.exe in French Win10 event
            - '= C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell'
            - '= C:\Windows\SysWOW64\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell'
            # In some cases powershell was invoked with inverted slashes
            - '= C:/Windows/System32/WindowsPowerShell/v1.0/powershell'
            - '= C:/Windows/SysWOW64/WindowsPowerShell/v1.0/powershell'
            # In some cases \??\C:.. is used
            - '= \\\?\?\C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell'
            - '= \\\?\?\C:\Windows\SysWOW64\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell'
    filter_sdiagnhost:
        ContextInfo|contains: '= C:\WINDOWS\System32\sdiagnhost.exe -Embedding' # When MSDT is launched for example
    filter_citrix:
        ContextInfo|contains: 'ConfigSyncRun.exe'
    filter_adace:  # Active Directory Administrative Center Enhancements
        ContextInfo|contains: 'C:\Windows\system32\dsac.exe'
    filter_winrm:
        ContextInfo|contains: 'C:\Windows\system32\wsmprovhost.exe -Embedding'
    filter_help_update:
        Payload|contains:
            - 'Update-Help'
            - 'Failed to update Help for the module'
    filter_wapshost:
        ContextInfo|contains: 'Host Name = WaPSHost'
    condition: selection and not 1 of filter_*

rules.title: Entra ID authentication strength change
rules.desc: Identifies when the allowed sign-in method combinations of a custom authentication strength are changed in Microsoft Entra ID. An authentication strength lists the method combinations that satisfy a Conditional Access policy, for example phishing-resistant methods only. An attacker with the Conditional Access Administrator role could add a weaker method to a strength that a policy already uses, so the policy stays in place but accepts weaker sign-ins. Creating or deleting a whole strength is no…
rules.query:
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where ingestion_time() > ago(1h)
| where OperationName =~ "Authentication Strength Policy Update"
| where Result !~ "failure"
| extend InitiatingAppName = tostring(InitiatedBy.app.displayName)
| extend InitiatingUserPrincipalName = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName)
| extend InitiatingAadUserId = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.id)
| extend InitiatingIPAddress = tostring(iff(isnotempty(InitiatedBy.user.ipAddress), InitiatedBy.user.ipAddress, InitiatedBy.app.ipAddress))
| extend InitiatingAccountName = tostring(split(InitiatingUserPrincipalName, "@")[0]), InitiatingAccountUPNSuffix = tostring(split(InitiatingUserPrincipalName, "@")[1])
| mv-apply Target = TargetResources on (
    mv-expand Property = Target.modifiedProperties
    | summarize PropertyBag = make_bag(bag_pack(tostring(Property.displayName), bag_pack("old", tostring(Property.oldValue), "new", tostring(Property.newValue))))
  )
| extend CombinationsBefore = trim('"', tostring(PropertyBag.AllowedCombinations.old))
| extend CombinationsAfter = trim('"', tostring(PropertyBag.AllowedCombinations.new))
| extend StrengthId = trim('"', tostring(PropertyBag.Id.new))
| where isnotempty(CombinationsAfter)
| mv-apply Combination = split(CombinationsBefore, "|") to typeof(string) on (
    extend Methods = strcat_array(array_sort_asc(split(replace_string(Combination, " ", ""), ",")), ",")
    | where isnotempty(Methods)
    | summarize NormalizedBefore = tostring(array_sort_asc(make_set(Methods)))
  )
| mv-apply Combination = split(CombinationsAfter, "|") to typeof(string) on (
    extend Methods = strcat_array(array_sort_asc(split(replace_string(Combination, " ", ""), ",")), ",")
    | where isnotempty(Methods)
    | summarize NormalizedAfter = tostring(array_sort_asc(make_set(Methods)))
  )
| where NormalizedBefore != NormalizedAfter
| project-away NormalizedBefore, NormalizedAfter
| project-reorder TimeGenerated, OperationName, StrengthId, CombinationsBefore, CombinationsAfter, InitiatingUserPrincipalName, InitiatingAppName, InitiatingIPAddress

rules.title: Entra ID security defaults disabled
rules.desc: Identifies when security defaults are turned off in Microsoft Entra ID. Security defaults require all users to register for MFA, require MFA for administrators and when necessary for users, protect access to the Azure portal and other management tools, and block legacy authentication and device code flow. An attacker with the Conditional Access Administrator role or higher can turn them off so that stolen passwords work without MFA. Turning them off is also a normal step when moving to Conditio…
rules.query:
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where ingestion_time() > ago(1h)
| where OperationName =~ "Update security defaults"
| where Result !~ "failure"
| extend InitiatingAppName = tostring(InitiatedBy.app.displayName)
| extend InitiatingAppServicePrincipalId = tostring(InitiatedBy.app.servicePrincipalId)
| extend InitiatingUserPrincipalName = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName)
| extend InitiatingAadUserId = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.id)
| extend InitiatingIPAddress = tostring(iff(isnotempty(InitiatedBy.user.ipAddress), InitiatedBy.user.ipAddress, InitiatedBy.app.ipAddress))
| extend InitiatingAccountName = tostring(split(InitiatingUserPrincipalName, "@")[0]), InitiatingAccountUPNSuffix = tostring(split(InitiatingUserPrincipalName, "@")[1])
| extend TargetResourceName = tostring(TargetResources[0].displayName)
| extend TargetResourceType = tostring(TargetResources[0].type)
| extend ModifiedProperties = TargetResources[0].modifiedProperties
| mv-apply Property = ModifiedProperties on (
    extend PropertyOld = parse_json(tostring(Property.oldValue)), PropertyNew = parse_json(tostring(Property.newValue))
    | where isnotempty(tostring(PropertyNew.isEnabled)) or isnotempty(tostring(PropertyOld.isEnabled))
    | project SecurityDefaultsEnabledBefore = tostring(PropertyOld.isEnabled), SecurityDefaultsEnabledAfter = tostring(PropertyNew.isEnabled)
    | extend IsDisableChange = iff(SecurityDefaultsEnabledAfter =~ "false" and not(SecurityDefaultsEnabledBefore =~ "false"), 1, 0)
    | top 1 by IsDisableChange desc
    | project-away IsDisableChange
  )
| where SecurityDefaultsEnabledAfter =~ "false"
| where not(SecurityDefaultsEnabledBefore =~ "false")
| project-reorder TimeGenerated, OperationName, TargetResourceName, TargetResourceType, SecurityDefaultsEnabledBefore, SecurityDefaultsEnabledAfter, InitiatingUserPrincipalName, InitiatingAppName, InitiatingIPAddress, ModifiedProperties

rules.title: External guest invitation followed by Microsoft Entra ID PowerShell signin
rules.desc: 'By default guests have capability to invite more external guest users, guests also can do suspicious Microsoft Entra ID enumeration. let queryfrequency = 1h;

| where TimeGenerated > ago(queryperiod)
| where OperationName in ("Invite external user", "Bulk invite users - started (bulk)", "Invite external user with reset invitation status")
| extend InitiatingAppName = tostring(InitiatedBy.app.displayName)
| extend InitiatingAppServicePrincipalId = tostring(InitiatedBy.app.servicePrincipalId)
| extend InitiatingUserPrincipalName = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName)

| extend InitiatingIpAddress = tostring(iff(isnotempty(InitiatedBy.user.ipAddress), InitiatedBy.user.ipAddress, InitiatedBy.app.ipAddress))

    parsedUser = replace_string(iff(UserToCompare startswith "live.com#", tostring(split(tolower(UserToCompare), "#")[1]), tostring(split(tolower(UserToCompare), "#ext#")[0])), "@", "_"),
    InvitationTime = TimeGenerated
| join (
    (union isfuzzy=true SigninLogs, AADNonInteractiveUserSignInLogs)
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(queryfrequency)
    | where UserType != "Member"
    | where AppId has_any                       // This web may contain a list of these apps: https://msshells.net/
        ("1b730954-1685-4b74-9bfd-dac224a7b894",// Azure Active Directory PowerShell

         "9bc3ab49-b65d-410a-85ad-de819febfddc",// Microsoft SharePoint Online Management Shell
         "12128f48-ec9e-42f0-b203-ea49fb6af367",// MS Teams Powershell Cmdlets

         "14d82eec-204b-4c2f-b7e8-296a70dab67e",// Microsoft Graph PowerShell

    | summarize arg_min(TimeGenerated, *) by UserPrincipalName

rules.title: High percentage of classical-only clients on PQC Engine
rules.desc: More than 50% of TLS handshakes on a PQC Engine instance in the last 24 hours were from classical-only clients that did not offer any post-quantum key exchange groups. These connections are not protected against harvest-now-decrypt-later attacks. Consider requiring PQC-capable TLS libraries or upgrading connecting services to OpenSSL 3.5+ or BoringSSL with ML-KEM support.
rules.query:
PQCEngine_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where EventType == "handshake"
| summarize Total = count(), Classical = countif(ClientClass in ("classical", "legacy")) by Hostname, InstanceId
| extend ClassicalPct = round(100.0 * Classical / Total, 1)
| where ClassicalPct > 50
| project Hostname, InstanceId, Total, Classical, ClassicalPct
| order by ClassicalPct desc

rules.title: KEM operation failure spike on PQC Engine
rules.desc: An elevated rate of KEM (Key Encapsulation Mechanism) operation failures was detected on a PQC Engine instance. This may indicate incompatible ML-KEM implementations between client and server, corrupted key material, memory constraints on the F5 BIG-IP, or a misconfigured PQC Engine provider. Investigate the failing algorithm and operation type.
rules.query:
PQCEngine_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where EventType == "kem_op"
| where Success == 0
| summarize FailureCount = count(), Algorithms = make_set(Algorithm, 5), Operations = make_set(Operation, 5) by Hostname, InstanceId
| where FailureCount > 5
| project Hostname, InstanceId, FailureCount, Algorithms, Operations
| order by FailureCount desc

rules.title: PQC downgrade on engine -- client offered hybrid but classical negotiated
rules.desc: A TLS handshake completed where the client offered post-quantum hybrid key exchange groups but the F5 BIG-IP negotiated a classical-only group. This may indicate PQC Engine misconfiguration, an intermediate device stripping PQC groups from the ClientHello, or the engine running in monitor mode rather than enforce mode. Investigate the negotiated vs offered groups.
rules.query:
PQCEngine_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where EventType == "handshake"
| where PQCOffered == 1 and PQCNegotiated == 0
| project TimeGenerated, Hostname, InstanceId, NegotiatedGroup, PeerGroups, CipherSuite, ClientClass, Detail
| order by TimeGenerated desc

rules.title: PQC Engine policy blocked a TLS handshake
rules.desc: The PQC Engine crypto policy enforcement blocked a TLS handshake that did not meet minimum requirements. This may indicate a client attempting to connect with banned cipher suites, blocked key exchange groups, or TLS versions below the policy minimum. Review the blocked algorithm and client to determine if policy adjustment or client upgrade is needed.
rules.query:
PQCEngine_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where EventType == "policy_block"
| project TimeGenerated, Hostname, InstanceId, Algorithm, NegotiatedGroup, CipherSuite, ClientClass, Detail
| order by TimeGenerated desc

rules.title: PQC Engine policy upgraded cipher selection
rules.desc: The PQC Engine policy engine upgraded the cipher selection for one or more TLS handshakes. This occurs when the engine is in enforce mode and the initial negotiation would have used a weaker algorithm than the policy allows. The engine intervened to select a stronger (typically PQ-hybrid) algorithm. This is an expected and positive signal when enforcement is enabled.
rules.query:
PQCEngine_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where EventType == "policy_upgrade"
| summarize UpgradeCount = count(), Algorithms = make_set(Algorithm, 10) by Hostname, InstanceId
| project Hostname, InstanceId, UpgradeCount, Algorithms
| order by UpgradeCount desc

rules.title: Vulnerable classical algorithm detected in TLS negotiation
rules.desc: The PQC Engine vulnerability database flagged a quantum-vulnerable algorithm during a TLS handshake or cryptographic operation on F5 BIG-IP. Algorithms such as RSA-2048, ECDSA P-256, or Ed25519 are vulnerable to Shor's algorithm on a cryptographically relevant quantum computer. Migrate to PQ-hybrid algorithms (X25519+ML-KEM-768) to protect against harvest-now-decrypt-later attacks.
rules.query:
PQCEngine_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where EventType == "vuln_detected"
| project TimeGenerated, Hostname, InstanceId, Algorithm, Operation, ClientClass, PQCOffered, Detail
| order by TimeGenerated desc

rules.title: High percentage of clients connecting without PQC support
rules.desc: Identifies PQC Proxy instances where more than 50% of TLS handshakes in the last 24 hours used classical (non-PQC) key exchange because clients did not offer any post-quantum groups. This is an adoption tracking signal - these clients are not protected against harvest-now-decrypt-later attacks. Consider requiring client TLS library upgrades or communicating PQC requirements to connecting services.
rules.query:
PQCProxy_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where EventType == "handshake"
| summarize Total = count(), Classical = countif(QuantumPosture == "classical") by ProxyHost, ProxyInstanceId
| where Classical * 100.0 / Total > 50
| extend ClassicalPct = round(100.0 * Classical / Total, 1)
| project ProxyHost, ProxyInstanceId, Total, Classical, ClassicalPct
| order by ClassicalPct desc

rules.title: PQC downgrade detected - client offered hybrid but classical was negotiated
rules.desc: Identifies TLS handshakes where the client offered a post-quantum hybrid key exchange group (X25519MLKEM768 or X25519Kyber768Draft00) but the negotiation fell back to a classical group (X25519 or P-256). This may indicate a misconfigured PQC Proxy, a middlebox stripping PQC groups from ClientHello, or an active downgrade attack. Investigate the proxy configuration and network path between client and proxy.
rules.query:
PQCProxy_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where EventType == "downgrade"
| project TimeGenerated, ProxyHost, ProxyInstanceId, ClientIP, NegotiatedGroup, OfferedGroups, CipherSuite, Metadata
| order by TimeGenerated desc

rules.title: PQC Proxy certificate expiring within 7 days - immediate renewal required
rules.desc: Identifies PQC Proxy instances serving a TLS certificate that expires within the next 7 days. Immediate certificate renewal is required to prevent service outage. Clients will receive TLS errors once the certificate expires, breaking all PQC-protected connections through the proxy.
rules.query:
PQCProxy_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where EventType == "cert_expiry"
| summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by ProxyInstanceId, CertPath
| where CertExpiryDays <= 7
| project TimeGenerated, ProxyHost, ProxyInstanceId, CertPath, CertExpiryDays, Metadata
| order by CertExpiryDays asc

rules.title: PQC Proxy certificate expiring within 30 days
rules.desc: Identifies PQC Proxy instances serving a TLS certificate that expires within the next 30 days. Certificate renewal should be performed before expiry to avoid service disruption. If the certificate is renewed, ensure the replacement uses a PQ-hybrid or classical algorithm compatible with TLS 1.3 and the configured key exchange groups.
rules.query:
PQCProxy_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where EventType == "cert_expiry"
| summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by ProxyInstanceId, CertPath
| where CertExpiryDays <= 30
| project TimeGenerated, ProxyHost, ProxyInstanceId, CertPath, CertExpiryDays, Metadata
| order by CertExpiryDays asc

rules.title: TLS handshake failure spike on PQC Proxy
rules.desc: Identifies an elevated rate of TLS handshake failures on a PQC Proxy instance within the last hour. This may indicate clients using incompatible TLS libraries, expired or invalid certificates, a denial-of-service attempt, or network-level interference with the TLS handshake. Investigate the error messages and client IPs to determine the root cause.
rules.query:
PQCProxy_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where EventType == "tls_error"
| summarize ErrorCount = count(), DistinctClients = dcount(ClientIP), Errors = make_set(ErrorMessage, 5) by ProxyHost, ProxyInstanceId
| where ErrorCount > 10
| project ProxyHost, ProxyInstanceId, ErrorCount, DistinctClients, Errors
| order by ErrorCount desc

rules.title: Upstream backend connection failures on PQC Proxy
rules.desc: Identifies PQC Proxy instances experiencing elevated upstream connection failures when forwarding requests to backend services. This may indicate the backend is down, overloaded, or unreachable. While the PQC Proxy TLS termination is functioning correctly, clients will receive 502/504 errors until the backend recovers.
rules.query:
PQCProxy_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where EventType == "upstream_error"
| summarize ErrorCount = count(), Errors = make_set(ErrorMessage, 5) by ProxyHost, ProxyInstanceId, UpstreamTarget
| where ErrorCount > 5
| project ProxyHost, ProxyInstanceId, UpstreamTarget, ErrorCount, Errors
| order by ErrorCount desc

rules.title: Linux Auditd Shell from Web or Application Directory
rules.desc: This analytic looks for a shell started with the "-c" argument for command line execution while its working directory is a web application directory. It joins auditd SYSCALL, EXECVE, and CWD records from the same event. A match may show that a web application ran a command, check the parent process and command before treating it as suspicious.
rules.logsource: Linux Auditd Syscall, Linux Auditd Execve
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali, Splunk
fp: Deployments, build steps, application jobs, and administrative scripts may run shells from a web application directory. Review the command argument, parent PID, service ownership, and nearby HTTP traffic. Hex-encoded EX…
rules.how: Install and enable auditd on Linux web servers and load the Neo23x0 audit.rules (https://github.com/Neo23x0/auditd/blob/master/audit.rules) ruleset, including the process_creation execve and execveat rules. Forward /var/log/audit/audit.log with the Splunk Universal Forwarder and install Splunk Add-…
rules.query:
`linux_auditd`
(
    (
        type=SYSCALL
        key="process_creation"
        success="yes"
        exe IN (
            "*/ash",
            "*/bash",
            "*/busybox",
            "*/csh",
            "*/dash",
            "*/fish",
            "*/ion",
            "*/ksh",
            "*/mksh",
            "*/sh",
            "*/tcsh",
            "*/zsh"
        )
    )
    OR
    (
        type=EXECVE
        a0 IN (
            "ash", "*/ash",
            "bash", "*/bash",
            "csh", "*/csh",
            "dash", "*/dash",
            "fish", "*/fish",
            "ion", "*/ion",
            "ksh", "*/ksh",
            "mksh", "*/mksh",
            "sh", "*/sh",
            "tcsh", "*/tcsh",
            "zsh", "*/zsh",
            "busybox", "*/busybox"
        )
    )
    OR
    (
        type=CWD
        cwd IN (
            "/app",
            "/app/*",
            "/dev/shm",
            "/dev/shm/*",
            "/home/*/*",
            "/home/*/*/*",
            "/opt/*",
            "/srv/http",
            "/srv/http/*",
            "/srv/www",
            "/srv/www/*",
            "/usr/share/nginx/html",
            "/usr/share/nginx/html/*",
            "/var/lib/tomcat*/webapps",
            "/var/lib/tomcat*/webapps/*",
            "/var/www",
            "/var/www/*"
        )
    )
)

| rex field=msg "audit\\((?<audit_event_id>[^)]+)\\)"

| eval shell_exec=if(
    type="SYSCALL"
    AND key="process_creation"
    AND success="yes"
    AND match(
        lower(exe),
        "(^|/)(ash|bash|busybox|csh|dash|fish|ion|ksh|mksh|sh|tcsh|zsh)$"
    ),
    1,
    0
)

| eval argv0=if(type="EXECVE",lower(a0),null())
| eval argv1=if(type="EXECVE",a1,null())

| eval shell_argv=if(
    type="EXECVE"
    AND (
        match(
            argv0,
            "(^|/)(ash|bash|csh|dash|fish|ion|ksh|mksh|sh|tcsh|zsh)$"
        )
        OR (
            match(argv0,"(^|/)busybox$")
            AND match(lower(argv1),"^(ash|sh)$")
        )
    ),
    1,
    0
)

| eval exec_args=if(
    type="EXECVE",
    mvappend(a1,a2,a3,a4,a5,a6,a7,a8),
    null()
)

| eval c_option_index=if(
    shell_argv=1,
    mvfind(exec_args,"(?i)^-[a-z]*c[a-z]*$"),
    null()
)

| eval fish_command_index=if(
    shell_argv=1 AND match(argv0,"(^|/)fish$"),
    mvfind(exec_args,"(?i)^--command(?:=.*)?$"),
    null()
)

| eval shell_command=if(
    shell_argv=1
    AND (
        c_option_index>=0
        OR fish_command_index>=0
    ),
    1,
    0
)

| eval command_arg=case(
    c_option_index>=0,
        mvindex(exec_args,c_option_index+1),

rules.title: Classical fallback - PQC VPN tunnel established without quantum protection
rules.desc: A WireGuard tunnel was established using classical X25519 key exchange because the remote peer does not support ML-KEM-768 hybrid key exchange. The PQC policy was set to "prefer" or "allow", so the connection was permitted but is NOT protected against harvest-now-decrypt-later attacks. All traffic through this tunnel can be recorded and decrypted by a future quantum computer. Upgrade the remote peer to support PQC VPN Overlay.
rules.query:
PQCVPNOverlay_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where EventType_s == "classical_fallback"
| project TimeGenerated, PeerID_s, PeerAddress_s, KeyExchange_s, PolicyMode_s, HNDLRisk_d, Metadata_s
| order by TimeGenerated desc

rules.title: High harvest-now-decrypt-later risk rate across VPN tunnels
rules.desc: More than 30% of active PQC VPN tunnels in the last 24 hours were established without quantum protection (HNDLRisk_d=1). Traffic through these tunnels is vulnerable to harvest-now-decrypt-later attacks. This is an adoption tracking signal -- review which peers lack PQC support and prioritize their upgrade to ML-KEM-768 hybrid key exchange.
rules.query:
PQCVPNOverlay_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where EventType_s == "tunnel_up"
| summarize Total = count(), AtRisk = countif(HNDLRisk_d == 1) by bin(TimeGenerated, 1d)
| extend HNDLPct = round(100.0 * AtRisk / Total, 1)
| where HNDLPct > 30
| project TimeGenerated, Total, AtRisk, HNDLPct

rules.title: New peer connected without PQC - quantum protection not available
rules.desc: A previously unseen peer was discovered and connected to the PQC VPN Overlay without post-quantum key exchange. This peer is using classical WireGuard only and traffic is vulnerable to harvest-now-decrypt-later. New peers should be provisioned with ML-KEM-768 hybrid key exchange support from the start to ensure quantum-safe connectivity.
rules.query:
let knownPeers = PQCVPNOverlay_CL
| where TimeGenerated between (ago(2d) .. ago(1d))
| distinct PeerID_s;
PQCVPNOverlay_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where EventType_s == "peer_discovered"
| where PQCUsed_d == 0
| where PeerID_s !in (knownPeers)
| project TimeGenerated, PeerID_s, PeerAddress_s, KeyExchange_s, PolicyMode_s, HNDLRisk_d

rules.title: Excessive tunnel rekeying on PQC VPN Overlay
rules.desc: An abnormally high number of session rekey events was detected for a peer within a short period. While periodic rekeying is expected (every ~120 seconds by default), a spike may indicate network instability, peer crashes and reconnects, or an attempt to exhaust KEM resources through repeated handshakes. Investigate the peer and network path.
rules.query:
PQCVPNOverlay_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where EventType_s == "tunnel_rekey"
| summarize RekeyCount = count() by PeerID_s, PeerAddress_s
| where RekeyCount > 20
| project PeerID_s, PeerAddress_s, RekeyCount
| order by RekeyCount desc

rules.title: PQC VPN tunnel handshake failure
rules.desc: A hybrid post-quantum WireGuard handshake failed. This may indicate key material incompatibility between peers, ML-KEM key encapsulation failure, network-level interference with the Noise IK handshake, or a peer running an incompatible PQC VPN Overlay version. Investigate the error message and peer address. Repeated failures from the same peer may indicate an attack or misconfiguration.
rules.query:
PQCVPNOverlay_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where EventType_s == "handshake_fail"
| project TimeGenerated, PeerID_s, PeerAddress_s, KeyExchange_s, PolicyMode_s, ErrorMessage_s, Metadata_s
| order by TimeGenerated desc

rules.title: PQC VPN policy blocked a connection
rules.desc: The PQC VPN Overlay policy engine blocked a peer connection. This occurs when PQCPolicy is set to "require" and a peer does not support hybrid post-quantum key exchange. The peer attempted to establish a classical WireGuard tunnel but was rejected because the policy mandates PQC protection. Either upgrade the remote peer to support ML-KEM-768 or change the policy to "prefer" to allow classical fallback.
rules.query:
PQCVPNOverlay_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where EventType_s == "policy_block"
| project TimeGenerated, PeerID_s, PeerAddress_s, KeyExchange_s, PolicyMode_s, PolicyAction_s, ErrorMessage_s
| order by TimeGenerated desc

rules.query:
`linux_auditd`

    type=ANOM_ABEND
    OR
    (
        type=SYSCALL success="yes"

            OR
            SYSCALL="execve"
        )
    )
)

| eval exe=coalesce(exe, executable), event_type=if(type="ANOM_ABEND", "crash", "start")
| eval sig=coalesce(sig, signal)

| where event_type="start" OR tonumber(sig) IN (6, 7, 11)

    $process.principal.hostname = $hostname
    $process.target.process.command_line = $command_line

    // cisa report referenced cmd /c in their report throughout, can filter this in/out for tuning as needed
    // other wmic switches like /user and /password, these have been excluded to focus on the commands being issued since local access does not require these
    (
        re.regex($process.target.process.command_line, `(^|[\\/])7z\b.*?\ba\b.*?\b-p.*?\bc:\\windows\\temp\\.*\.7z`) nocase or

        re.regex($process.target.process.command_line, `(^|[\\/])(cmd(\.exe)?|cmdbak)\b.*?[/c]\b.*?\bdir\b.*?\b127\.0\.0\.1\\c\$.*?/od`) nocase or
        re.regex($process.target.process.command_line, `(^|[\\/])ping\b.*?\b-a\b.*?\b-n\b.*?\b1\b`) nocase or
        re.regex($process.target.process.command_line, `(^|[\\/])wmic\b.*?\bprocess\b.*?\bcall\b.*?\bcreate\b.*?\bnet\b.*?\bstop\b.*?\bC:\\Windows\\Temp\\tmp\.log"`) nocase or
        re.regex($process.target.process.command_line, `\\ADMIN\$\\__.*2>&1`) nocase or
        //The following line could be swapped for the previous line for a looser match, but potentially noisier
        //re.regex($process.target.process.command_line, `\\ADMIN\$\\__`) nocase or
        re.regex($process.target.process.command_line, `(^|[\\/])net\b.*?\buse\b.*?\b127\.0\.0\.1\\ipc\$.*?/y.*?/d`) nocase or
        re.regex($process.target.process.command_line, `(^|[\\/])powershell\b.*?\bstart-process\b.*?\b-filepath\b.*?\bc:\\windows\\temp\\.*\.bat\b.*?\b-windowstyle\b.*?\bHidden`) nocase or
        re.regex($process.target.process.command_line, `(^|[\\/])rar\.exe\b.*?\ba\b.*?\bc:\\Windows\\temp\\.*?D:\\`) nocase or
        re.regex($process.target.process.command_line, `(^|[\\/])wmic\b.*?\b(cmd(\.exe)?|cmdbak)\b.*?[/c]\b.*?\bwhoami`) nocase or
        re.regex($process.target.process.command_line, `(^|[\\/])xcopy\b.*?\bc:\\windows\\temp\\hp\b.*?\bd:\\`) nocase

    $principal_process_pid = array_distinct($process.principal.process.pid)

rules.title: Java Base64 Decoder Argument Exceptions
rules.desc: The analytic finds Java Base64 decoder references and argument exceptions on the same JVM process within one minute. JIT messages add context when present. These logs indicate decoder activity and errors, but do not prove that a native overwrite or code execution occurred.
rules.logsource: Java HotSpot Exceptions, Java HotSpot JIT
rules.author: Onur Mustafa Erdogan, Nasreddine Bencherchali, Splunk
fp: Applications that routinely decode malformed Base64 can produce these events. The decoder and exception may come from separate requests within the same minute; review the surrounding application and network events.
rules.how: Configure java_hotspot_exceptions and java_hotspot_jit for the indexes and sourcetypes in your environment. A stock HotSpot JVM does not create exception or JIT log files; its default unified logging sends warning and error messages to stdout. Tomcat JULI logs under CATALINA_BASE/logs, Spring Boot'…
rules.query:
(`java_hotspot_jit` OR `java_hotspot_exceptions`)
(
    "*Input byte array has wrong*"
    OR "*IllegalArgumentException*"
    OR "*Base64$Decoder*"
    OR "*java/util/Base64*"
    OR "*OSR invalidation of lower level*"
)

| rex field=_raw "^\[(?<jvm_event_time_raw>[^\]]+)\]\[(?<jvm_pid_raw>\d+)\]\[(?<jvm_level_raw>[^\]]+)\]\[(?<jvm_tags_raw>[^\]]+)\]\s*(?<jvm_message_raw>.*)"

| eval process_id=coalesce(jvm_pid_raw,jvm_pid,process_id),
    jvm_message=coalesce(jvm_message_raw,jvm_message),
    event_time=_time

| where isnotnull(process_id)

| rex mode=sed field=jvm_message "s/0x[0-9A-Fa-f]{8,16}/0xXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX/g"
| rex mode=sed field=jvm_message "s/\s+bci\s+\d+\s+/ bci XXX /g"
| rex mode=sed field=jvm_message "s/^\d+\s+/XXXX /g"

| eval has_argument=if(match(jvm_message,"(?i)Input byte array has wrong|IllegalArgumentException"),1,0),
    has_decoder=if(match(jvm_message,"Base64[$]Decoder|java/util/Base64|Input byte array has wrong 4-byte ending unit"),1,0)

| eval reason=case(
    match(jvm_message,"(?i)Input byte array has wrong"),"Tailing byte exception",
    match(jvm_message,"(?i)OSR invalidation of lower level"),"JIT activity",
    has_decoder==1,"Base64 decoder reference",
    has_argument==1,"Argument exception"
)

| bin _time span=1m

| stats count
        min(event_time) AS firstTime
        max(event_time) AS lastTime
        max(has_argument) AS has_argument
        max(has_decoder) AS has_decoder
        values(sourcetype) AS sourcetype
        dc(sourcetype) AS dc_sourcetype
        values(source) AS source
        dc(source) AS dc_source
        values(reason) AS reason
        values(jvm_message) AS jvm_message
        BY _time host process_id

| where has_argument==1 AND has_decoder==1

| rename host AS dest

| fields - has_argument has_decoder

| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| `java_base64_decoder_argument_exceptions_filter`

rules.title: Java Base64 Exception With Process or File Activity
rules.desc: The analytic finds Base64-related Java argument exceptions near a process spawned by Java or a file created by Java on the same host and JVM PID.
rules.logsource: Java HotSpot Exceptions, Sysmon for Linux EventID 1
rules.author: Onur Mustafa Erdogan, Nasreddine Bencherchali, Splunk
fp: Java applications may decode malformed inputs while independently creating files or child processes. One-minute bins can also miss events at a minute boundary or associate unrelated activity on a busy JVM. Review the pr…
rules.how: Configure java_hotspot_exceptions and sysmon_linux for the indexes and sourcetypes in your environment. HotSpot exception diagnostics have no default file location. Tomcat's CATALINA_BASE/logs, Spring Boot's default console output, and Elasticsearch's application log directory do not supply this JV…
rules.query:
(
    `java_hotspot_exceptions`
    (
        "*Input byte array has wrong*"
        OR
        "*IllegalArgumentException*"
        OR
        "*Base64$Decoder*"
        OR
        "*java/util/Base64*"
    )
)
OR
(
    `sysmon_linux`
    (
        (EventID=1 ParentImage="*/java")
        OR
        (
            EventID=11
            Image="*/java"
            NOT TargetFilename IN ("*/_state/*","*/indices/*")
        )
    )
)
| rex field=_raw "^\[(?<jvm_event_time_raw>[^\]]+)\]\[(?<jvm_pid_raw>\d+)\]\[(?<jvm_level_raw>[^\]]+)\]\[(?<jvm_tags_raw>[^\]]+)\]\s*(?<jvm_message_raw>.*)"

| eval event_time=_time,
       jvm_message=coalesce(jvm_message_raw,jvm_message),
       observed_host=coalesce(host,Computer,dest),
       process_id=case(
            isnotnull(jvm_pid_raw),tostring(jvm_pid_raw),
            isnotnull(jvm_pid),tostring(jvm_pid),
            EventID==1,tostring(ParentProcessId),
            EventID==11,tostring(ProcessId)
        )
| where isnotnull(observed_host) AND isnotnull(process_id)

| rex mode=sed field=jvm_message "s/0x[0-9A-Fa-f]{8,16}/0xXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX/g"
| rex mode=sed field=jvm_message "s/\s+bci\s+\d+\s+/ bci XXX /g"
| rex mode=sed field=jvm_message "s/^\d+\s+/XXXX /g"

| eval has_argument=if(match(jvm_message,"(?i)Input byte array has wrong|IllegalArgumentException"),1,0),
       has_decoder=if(match(jvm_message,"Base64[$]Decoder|java/util/Base64|Input byte array has wrong 4-byte ending unit"),1,0),
       has_activity=if(EventID==1 OR EventID==11,1,0)

| eval activity=case(
      EventID==1,"Java spawned a process",
      EventID==11,"Java created a file"
  ),
  process_name=if(EventID==1,Image,null()),
  process=if(EventID==1,CommandLine,null()),
  file_path=if(EventID==11,TargetFilename,null()),
  file_name=if(EventID==11,mvindex(split(TargetFilename,"/"),-1),null())

| bin _time span=1m

| stats count
        min(event_time) AS firstTime
        max(event_time) AS lastTime
        max(has_argument) AS has_argument
        max(has_decoder) AS has_decoder
        max(has_activity) AS has_activity
        values(sourcetype) AS sourcetype
        dc(sourcetype) AS dc_sourcetype
        values(activity) AS activity
        values(jvm_message) AS jvm_message
        values(process_name) AS process_name
        values(process) AS process
        values(file_name) AS file_name
        values(file_path) AS file_path
        BY _time observed_host process_id

| where has_argument==1 AND has_decoder==1 AND has_activity==1

| rename observed_host AS dest

| eval reason="Java Base64 exception observed with ".mvjoin(activity," and ")

| fields - has_argument has_decoder has_activity activity

| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| `java_base64_exception_with_process_or_file_activity_filter`

process_name IN (

    "*g++*",
    "*gcc*",
    "cc",
    "cc1",
    "cc1plus",
    "tcc"

process IN (

rules.title: Linux Suspicious Namespace Creation
rules.desc: The following analytic detects an unprivileged user invoking the unshare syscall with user namespace flags followed within 120 seconds by a root-owned shell or interpreter spawning under the same parent process, correlating auditd syscall telemetry with Sysmon process creation events to identify the two-step sequence characteristic of user-namespace-based Linux kernel privilege escalation exploits such as DirtyFrag.
rules.logsource: Linux Auditd Syscall, Sysmon for Linux EventID 1
rules.author: Raven Tait, Splunk
fp: No false positives have been identified at this time.
rules.how: To implement this detection, the process begins by ingesting auditd data, that consist SYSCALL, TYPE, EXECVE and PROCTITLE events, which captures command-line executions and process details on Unix/Linux systems. These logs should be ingested and processed using Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux (ht…
rules.query:
type=SYSCALL SYSCALL=unshare
| where uid != "0" AND uid != "4294967295"
| where a0 IN ("10000000","50000000","70000000","10020000","50020000","70020000")
| eval unshare_time=_time,
      unshare_pid=pid,
      unshare_ppid=ppid,
      trigger_uid=uid,
      trigger_auid=auid,
      trigger_exe=exe,
      ns_flags=a0
| table host, unshare_time, comm, syscall, unshare_pid, unshare_ppid,
        trigger_uid, trigger_auid, trigger_exe, ns_flags
| join type=inner host unshare_ppid [
    search `sysmon_linux` EventID=1 User=root
    | where match(Image, "/(su|sudo|pkexec|passwd|chsh|newgrp|doas|run0|sg|dash|sh|bash|zsh|fish|ksh|csh|tcsh|ash|mksh|busybox|tmux|screen|node|python[^/]*|perl[^/]*|ruby[^/]*|php[^/]*|lua[^/]*)$")
    | eval root_spawn_time=_time, root_pid=ProcessId,
          root_exe=Image, root_cmdline=CommandLine, root_parent=ParentProcessId
    | rename ParentProcessId AS unshare_ppid
    | table host, unshare_ppid, root_spawn_time, root_pid,
            root_exe, root_cmdline, root_parent, unshare_time,
            action, original_file_name, parent_process, parent_process_exec,
            parent_process_guid, parent_process_id, parent_process_name,
            parent_process_path, process, process_exec, process_guid,
            process_hash, process_id, process_integrity_level,
            process_name, process_path, user, user_id, vendor_product
]
| where (root_spawn_time - unshare_time) >= 0
| where (root_spawn_time - unshare_time) <= 120
| eval elapsed_sec=round(root_spawn_time - unshare_time, 2)
| eval ioc_match=case(
    ns_flags="50000000", "dirtyfrag (CLONE_NEWUSER|CLONE_NEWNET)",
    ns_flags="10000000", "CLONE_NEWUSER only",
    ns_flags="70000000", "CLONE_NEWUSER|CLONE_NEWNET|CLONE_NEWPID",
    1=1, "namespace flags="+ns_flags

| rename host as dest
| stats
    count                              AS count,
    min(unshare_time)                  AS firstTime,
    max(unshare_time)                  AS lastTime,
    values(trigger_uid)                AS trigger_uid,
    values(trigger_auid)               AS trigger_auid,
    values(trigger_exe)                AS trigger_exe,
    values(ns_flags)                   AS ns_flags,
    values(ioc_match)                  AS ioc_match,
    values(unshare_pid)                AS unshare_pid,
    values(unshare_ppid)               AS unshare_ppid,
    values(root_exe)                   AS root_exe,
    values(root_cmdline)               AS root_cmdline,
    values(root_pid)                   AS root_pid,
    values(elapsed_sec)                AS elapsed_sec,
    values(process_hash)               AS process_hash,
    values(vendor_product)             AS vendor_product
    by dest, comm, syscall
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| `linux_suspicious_namespace_creation_filter`

rule sap_btp_subaccount_deleted {

  meta:
    author = "Google Cloud Security"
    description = "A BTP subaccount entity was deleted from the global account"
    severity = "High"
    tactic = "TA0040"
    technique = "T1485"

  events:
    $e.metadata.log_type = "SAP_BTP"

    $e.security_result.detection_fields["object_id_entity"] = "com.sap.core.commercial.service.accounts.model.Subaccount"
    (
      $e.security_result.detection_fields["new_stateDetails"] = "DELETE_SUBACCOUNT_ENTITY" nocase or
      $e.security_result.detection_fields["new_entityState"] = /^(DELETING|DELETED)$/ nocase
    )

    $user = strings.coalesce($e.principal.user.user_display_name, $e.principal.user.userid)
    $subaccount_guid = $e.security_result.detection_fields["new_guid"]

  match:
    $user, $subaccount_guid over 1h

  outcome:
    $risk_score = max(
      if($e.security_result.detection_fields["new_usedForProduction"] = "NOT_USED_FOR_PRODUCTION", 70, 95)
    )
    $principal_user = array_distinct($user)
    $subaccount_name = array_distinct($e.security_result.detection_fields["new_displayName"])
    $subaccount_subdomain = array_distinct($e.security_result.detection_fields["new_subdomain"])
    $subaccount_id = array_distinct($e.security_result.detection_fields["new_id"])
    $subaccount_region = array_distinct($e.security_result.detection_fields["new_region"])
    $used_for_production = array_distinct($e.security_result.detection_fields["new_usedForProduction"])
    $entity_state = array_distinct($e.security_result.detection_fields["new_entityState"])
    $state_details = array_distinct($e.security_result.detection_fields["new_stateDetails"])
    $last_modified_by = array_distinct($e.security_result.detection_fields["new_lastModifiedBy"])
    $global_account_tenant = array_distinct($e.security_result.detection_fields["tenant"])
    $audit_category = array_distinct($e.security_result.category_details)
    $event_count = count_distinct($e.metadata.id)

  condition:
    $e
}

rule sap_btp_tenant_audit_log_silent {

/*
- this rule should be used in conjunction with a silent feed alert, and is only meant to alert on specific tenants going silent
- this rule will only fire once per outage
*/

  meta:
    author = "Google Cloud Security"
    display_name = "SAP BTP Tenant Audit Log Stream Interrupted"
    description = "An SAP BTP tenant that was recently active stopped producing audit logs"
    severity = "High"
    tactic = "TA0005"
    technique = "T1562.008"

  events:
    //creates a list of tenants that have logs greater than 1 hour ago
    $historical.metadata.log_type = "SAP_BTP"
    $historical.security_result.detection_fields["tenant"] = $tenant
    $historical.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds <= timestamp.current_seconds() - 3600

    //creates a list of tenants that have logs within the last hour
    $recent.metadata.log_type = "SAP_BTP"
    $recent.security_result.detection_fields["tenant"] = $tenant
    $recent.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds > timestamp.current_seconds() - 3600

  match:
    //aggregate by tenant
    $tenant over 3h

  outcome:
    $risk_score         = 80
    $last_log_time      = max($historical.metadata.event_timestamp.seconds)
    $historical_records = count_distinct($historical.security_result.detection_fields["message_uuid"])

  condition:
    //checks if that tenant has logs greater than 1 hour old, but not within the most recent hour
    $historical and !$recent
}

rule sap_bulk_download_following_restricted_object_access {

  meta:
    author = "Google Cloud Security"
    description = "A user downloaded a large volume of data shortly after accessing a restricted table, program, or transaction"
    severity = "Critical"
    tactic = "TA0010"
    technique = "T1020"

  events:
    $access.metadata.log_type = "SAP_SECURITY_AUDIT"
    $access.principal.user.userid = $user
    $access.target.application = $target_sid

    (
      (
        $access.additional.fields["msg_1"] = /^(DU9|CUZ)$/ and
        $access.additional.fields["param1_1"] in %sap_sensitive_tables.name
      ) or
      (
        $access.additional.fields["msg_1"] = "AUW" and
        $access.additional.fields["param1_1"] in %sap_sensitive_abap_programs.abap_program
      ) or
      (
        $access.additional.fields["msg_1"] = /^(AU3|AU4)$/ and
        (
          $access.security_result.detection_fields["slgtc_1"] in %sap_sensitive_transactions.transaction_code or
          $access.additional.fields["param1_1"] in %sap_sensitive_transactions.transaction_code
        )
      )
    )

    $download.metadata.log_type = "SAP_SECURITY_AUDIT"
    $download.additional.fields["msg_1"] = "AUY"
    $download.principal.user.userid = $user
    $download.target.application = $target_sid

  match:
    $user, $target_sid over 6h after $access

  outcome:
    $risk_score = 90
    $source_user = array_distinct($user)
    $target_system = array_distinct($target_sid)
    $total_bytes_downloaded = sum(cast.as_int(re.replace($download.additional.fields["param1_1"], ",", "")))
    $download_paths = array_distinct($download.additional.fields["param3_1"])
    $terminal_ip = array_distinct($download.principal.ip)
    $sap_client = array_distinct($download.target.resource.attribute.labels["slgmand_1"])
    $accessed_objects = array_distinct($access.additional.fields["param1_1"])
    $executed_programs = array_distinct($access.principal.process.file.names)
    $executed_tcodes = array_distinct($access.security_result.detection_fields["slgtc_1"])

  condition:
    $access and $download and $total_bytes_downloaded > 800000
}

rule sap_credential_reset_followed_by_use_from_shared_ip {

  meta:
    author = "Google Cloud Security"
    description = "A privileged account's credentials were reset and then used from an IP the resetting account had also used"
    severity = "High"
    tactic = "TA0004"
    technique = "T1098"

events:
    $mod.metadata.log_type = "SAP_SECURITY_AUDIT"

    (
      (
        $mod.additional.fields["msg_1"] = "BU2" and
        $changed_user = $mod.additional.fields["param2_1"]
      ) or (
        $mod.additional.fields["msg_1"] = "AUD" and
        $changed_user = $mod.additional.fields["param1_1"]
      )
    )

    $actor = $mod.principal.user.userid
    $actor != $changed_user
    $sid = $mod.target.application

    $client = $mod.target.resource.attribute.labels["slgmand_1"]

    not $actor in %SAP_ChangeUserMasterDataExcludedUsers.userid

    $changed_user in %sap_admin_users.user

    // the actor logging on
    $login_actor.metadata.log_type = "SAP_SECURITY_AUDIT"
    $login_actor.additional.fields["msg_1"] = /^(AU1|AU5)$/
    $actor = $login_actor.principal.user.userid
    $shared_ip = $login_actor.principal.ip
    $sid = $login_actor.target.application
    $client = $login_actor.target.resource.attribute.labels["slgmand_1"]

    // the changed user logging on from the same IP
    $login_changed.metadata.log_type = "SAP_SECURITY_AUDIT"
    $login_changed.additional.fields["msg_1"] = /^(AU1|AU5)$/
    $changed_user = $login_changed.principal.user.userid
    $shared_ip = $login_changed.principal.ip
    $sid = $login_changed.target.application
    $client = $login_changed.target.resource.attribute.labels["slgmand_1"]

  match:
    $actor, $changed_user, $sid, $client, $shared_ip over 48h after $mod

  outcome:
    $risk_score = 85
    $source_actor = array_distinct($actor)
    $changed_user_final = array_distinct($changed_user)
    $target_sid = array_distinct($sid)
    $sap_client = array_distinct($client)
    $shared_terminal_ip = array_distinct($shared_ip)
    $log_description = array_distinct($mod.metadata.description)
    $instance = array_distinct($mod.target.resource.name)

  condition:
    $mod and $login_actor and $login_changed
}

    $ip = $e.principal.ip

    $ip != ""

    $client, $ip over 15m

    $target_sid = array_distinct($e.target.application)
    $audit_class = array_distinct($e.security_result.summary)
